name: Almond Milk (Unsweetened)
land_types_note: Irrigated Mediterranean-climate orchards, ~80% in California's Central Valley.
sentient_harm_explanation: Commercial almond orchards depend on trucked-in honeybee colonies (roughly two-thirds of all US managed hives each February) for pollination; the resulting hive stress, pesticide exposure and elevated bee mortality are an indirect harm shared by every product made from these almonds, including this milk.

source.title: USDA FoodData Central — Almond Milk, Unsweetened, Plain, Shelf Stable (Foundation Foods)
source.note: Unsweetened almond milk (id 69) — USDA FDC Foundation Foods fdcId 1999631, per-100g analytical values converted to per-gram: 14.56 kcal, 1.221 g fat, 0.104 g sat fat, 0.555 g protein, 0 g fiber, 59.58 mg sodium, 0.337 g carbs, 0 g sugar, 0 cholesterol/trans fat. Values reflect the fortified, ready-to-drink product as purchased (calcium carbonate, vitamin D/E, sunflower lecithin, gellan/locust bean gum added; no added sugar).

source.note: Almond milk (id 69) — yield_fraction: set to 1 because the nutrition values above are already for the ready-to-drink product as purchased/consumed (no further inedible removal), matching how the almonds entry (id 1) treats its shelled-kernel nutrition basis.

source.title: FoodNavigator-USA — Almond Milk Only Contains 2% Almonds, Claims Lawsuit v. Blue Diamond (2015)
source.note: CORRECTION 2026-09-26: replaced 20,348 (OWID/P&N direct almond-milk land figure, source 341). That figure implies ~15% almond content, but this entry's calories, protein and water all imply ~2.5% (e.g. 0.1456/5.79 kcal/g = 2.5%), so it overstated land (and the yield-driven insect/bee/worm harm) ~6x relative to the almonds entry. New value = almonds yield_kg_ha (id 1, 3,000 kg/ha) ÷ 2.5% almond content (midpoint of the commonly cited 2–3%) = 120,000 kg almond milk/ha, consistent with how water_per_kg is derived.

source.title: Our World in Data — Environmental Footprint of Dairy and Plant-Based Milks (Poore & Nemecek 2018 meta-analysis)
source.note: Almond milk (id 69) — water_per_kg: OWID direct almond-milk figure, 371.45932 L per litre (Poore & Nemecek 2018 meta-analysis) ÷ 1.01 kg/L density = 367.78 L/kg. World/untagged. CROSS-CHECK: almonds' world water_per_kg (id 1, 13,080 L/kg, source 30/67, Mekonnen & Hoekstra) × ~2.5% almond content (source 342) = ~327 L/kg — within ~12% of the direct OWID figure, a reasonable consistency check (unlike the land-use figure above).

Not a directly published almond-milk-specific US figure; derived cross-check consistent in order of magnitude with the world OWID value.

No almond-milk-specific green/blue/grey breakdown is published, so the split is estimated by applying the parent crop's proportions to the directly measured total.

source.note: Almond milk (id 69) — availability_gg: rough estimate from web-search-aggregated market-research figures (Persistence Market Research / TechSci-style industry reports), not a verified primary statistic. Global almond-milk volume estimated at ~2.2 billion litres/yr (2023) × 1.01 kg/L density = ~2,222,000 t = 2,222 gg. Cross-check: US plant-based-milk retail sales were ~337.7 million gallons (~1,278 million L) in 2023 with almond milk at ~55-59% share → ~730-750 million L US (~750 gg); other estimates for the US ranged as low as ~400 million L to as high as ~850 million L, reflecting real inconsistency across market-research sources. Confidence 1 — flagged for replacement with a verified industry-association or USDA ERS figure if one becomes available.
